name: Sodium bicarbonate/potassium citrate/citric acid (urinary alkaliniser)
searchTerms: sodium bicarbonate potassium citrate citric acid

formulations.label: Granules (sachet)
formulations.strengths: UK comparator products: potassium citrate 3 g per sachet (granules); potassium citrate 1.5 g per 5 ml (oral solution)
formulations.note: The clinic product is listed as sodium bicarbonate with potassium citrate and citric acid. No UK product with this combination was found. This entry uses UK SmPCs for potassium citrate-only granules and oral solution, so it covers only the potassium citrate content (potassium load and the urine-alkalinising effect of citrate). It does NOT cover the sodium bicarbonate (sodium load) or citric acid content, and the UK products' doses, excipients and sodium statements do not apply to the clinic product. Use the clinic product label for dose and check its exact ingredients.

src.q: Potassium Citrate 3.0 g
Potassium Citrate 1.5g/5ml.

items.t: Symptomatic relief of mild urinary tract infection (cystitis), including dysuria.

src.q: For the symptomatic relief of mild urinary tract infections (cystitis).
For the symptomatic relief of dysuria associated with mild urinary tract infections, especially cystitis.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions in the two UK potassium citrate SmPCs checked.

dosing.note: No UK SmPC for the clinic combination product. The UK potassium citrate-only products have different contents, so their doses are not given here. Use the clinic product label.

items.t: UK potassium citrate granules: not recommended for children under 6 years. (Applies to the UK potassium citrate-only product; no UK data for the clinic combination.)

src.q: Not recommended for children under six years of age.

items.t: UK potassium citrate oral solution (differs): gives a dose for children from 1 year. Doses of the UK products do not apply to the clinic product.

src.q: Children 1 - 6 years: 5ml.

items.t: Oral solution SmPC: hyperkalaemia, renal dysfunction, ventricular arrhythmias and Addison's disease.

src.q: Contraindicated in hyperkalaemia, renal dysfunction, ventricular arrhythmics and Addison's Disease.

src.q: There are no specific contraindications but use with caution in patients with impaired renal function or cardiac disease.

items.t: Potassium load: hyperkalaemia may occur with prolonged high dosage (UK potassium citrate granules; each UK 3 g sachet contains 27.8 mmol K+). Check the potassium content of the clinic product.

src.q: (Each Cystopurin sachet contains 27.8 mmol K+)
Hyperkalaemia may occur on prolonged high dosage.

items.t: Renal or cardiac dysfunction and the elderly: use with caution.

src.q: It should be used with caution when renal or cardiac dysfunction is present.
Use with caution in the elderly

items.t: Symptomatic relief only, not antibacterial: co-prescribe effective antibacterial therapy (oral solution SmPC). Short-term use; see a doctor if symptoms persist after 48 hours (granules SmPC).

src.q: Potassium Citrate Mixture provides symptomatic relief only and is not anti-bacterial.
Effective anti-bacterial therapy should be co-prescribed.
Patients should seek doctor's advice if symptoms persist after 48 hours treatment.

items.t: Hyperkalaemia risk with potassium-sparing diuretics, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin-II receptor antagonists, other potassium-containing medicines, aliskiren, ciclosporin and tacrolimus.

src.q: Concurrent administration of the following drugs may lead to hyperkalaemia: potassium sparing diuretics, ACE inhibitors, aliskiren, angiotensin-II receptor antagonists, ciclosporin and tacrolimus.

Concurrent administration of potassium-containing drugs, potassium sparing diuretics or other drugs that increase potassium levels (e.g. ACE inhibitors, ciclosporin, aliskiren) may lead to hyperkalaemia.

items.t: Methenamine: avoid concomitant use (granules SmPC). Urine alkalinisation reduces the antibacterial activity of nitrofurantoin and methenamine (oral solution SmPC).

src.q: Avoid concomitant use with methenamine.
Particularly noteworthy is the diminished anti-bacterial activity of nitrofurantoin and methenamine.

items.t: Urine alkalinisation may increase renal clearance of acidic drugs (salicylates, tetracyclines, barbiturates) and prolong the half-life of basic drugs (sympathomimetics, stimulants).

src.q: Citrates alkalinise the urine and thus may alter the urinary excretion of a number of drugs.
This may lead to increased renal clearance of acidic drugs, such as salicylates, tetracylines and barbiturates
prolongation of the half-life of basic drugs, such as sympathomimetics and stimulants

items.t: Cardiac glycosides: possible interaction (activity depends partly on serum potassium); caution advised.

src.q: Therefore, there is a possible interaction and caution is advised.

items.t: Oral solution SmPC: contraindicated in renal dysfunction. Granules SmPC: use with caution in impaired renal function. No eGFR/CrCl threshold given.

src.q: Contraindicated in hyperkalaemia, renal dysfunction, ventricular arrhythmics and Addison's Disease.
There are no specific contraindications but use with caution in patients with impaired renal function or cardiac disease.

hepatic.note: No hepatic impairment statements in the two UK potassium citrate SmPCs checked.

items.t: Granules SmPC: no adequate evidence of safety but long use without apparent harm; use only if there is no safer alternative. Pregnant women should seek medical advice rather than self-treat cystitis.

src.q: If drug therapy is needed in pregnancy, this drug can be used if there is no safer alternative.
pregnant women should be advised to seek medical advice on the treatment of cystitis rather than using OTC medicines
